input.question: Why did the UK not invade the Faroe Islands/Iceland after the defeat of napoleon and his allies (Including the kingdom of Denmark-Norway).
input.ground_truth: Why would they want to? If they wanted naval bases facing the North Sea they were spoilt for choice in Scotland, and there's certainly no economic reason to annex these worthless islands. Although they had a lot of diplomatic capital, they were still negotiating, not dictating, the peace settlement; better to concentrate on areas with some sort of economic or strategic importance.

But even though the UK won the big game, they didn’t want to take the islands away from Denmark-Norway. Why? Because:

3. Denmark-Norway was now a friend of the UK, and they got along.

So, the UK just let Denmark-Norway keep the islands.
